_comment: Manifest for the Phase-4a ranking-evals corpus. Maps each resume fixture
id (== filename stem under fixtures/resumes/) to its expected ranking tag.
Kept deliberately separate from the resume fixtures themselves so a coder
can't quietly relabel a fixture to make a metric pass.
Tags: 'strong' / 'borderline' / 'weak' / 'adversarial'.
- strong / borderline: expected to surface in the top-k shortlist.
- weak: honestly lacks most required skills; must NOT surface in top-k.
- adversarial: a keyword-stuffer that lists every required/nice-to-have
skill by name but whose cited chunks carry no real supporting text
for those claims (see 'adversarial_type'). A correct anti-fabrication
evidence verifier (>= MatchWeights.evidence_verify_fuzz against the
cited chunk) must fail to verify these quotes, so this resume must
NOT surface in top-k even though its keyword overlap with the JD is
the highest of the whole corpus.
JDExtracted has no 'seniority' or per-skill 'is_must_have' field (see
core/src/schemas/jobs.py): every entry in the JD's required_skills is an
implicit must-have for stage-2 structured skill scoring; entries in
nice_to_have_skills feed stage-3 evidence text only, per the
'NICE_TO_HAVE skills' decision recorded in docs/EXTRACTION_PLAN.md.
--- Phase-4a strengthening additions (adequacy-review round 1) ---
must_not_surface_in_topk: true on every 'weak'/'adversarial' entry -- the
backstop the ranking-evals gate enforces against thresholds.toml's
[adversarial].must_not_surface_in_topk / [evidence].min_completeness_in_topk
once Phase 4c lands (see docs/adr for the invariant). NOT computed here.
expected_rank_band: {min, max} the tag implies for a CORRECT ranker's
output order (max=null means unbounded / 'anywhere below the top tier').
Bands are per-TAG canonical ranges (every 'strong' entry shares the same
band). The three QUALITY tiers stay strictly ordered; the adversarial
bait's band overlaps borderline/weak by exactly one displaced rank slot
(round-4 note below -- that overlap is arithmetic, and it is gated).
See the round-2 + round-4 notes below for how the numbers are derived.
gold_evidence: for a couple of 'strong' fixtures, skill.name -> the EXACT
substring of that skill's cited chunk text a correct evidence verifier
should quote. 4c's fuzz-boundary test perturbs these toward ~0.83
(must fail >= evidence_verify_fuzz) and ~0.87 (must pass). Fixture-only;
no scoring logic here.
--- Phase-4a FALSIFIABILITY hardening (round 3) ---
negative_evidence: chunk_id -> a FABRICATED quote that a correct
anti-fabrication verifier MUST FAIL to verify against that chunk (score
< MatchWeights.evidence_verify_fuzz), so the quote is blanked and never
surfaces. Every gold_evidence anchor is an exact substring and so
verifies at 1.0 -- which means thresholds.toml's
[evidence].verification_rate_min = 1.0 was satisfiable by a verifier
that returns True unconditionally. These negative anchors are what make
the anti-fabrication invariant falsifiable IN-CORPUS instead of deferred
to 4c on trust. r01/r02 carry both gold AND negative anchors, so the
verifier must DISCRIMINATE rather than reject (or accept) everything;
r09's is the fabrication its whole fixture exists to bait. Gated by
thresholds.toml's [evidence].negative_evidence_must_fail.
r17_harper_nakamura: the ADR-007 F1-R format-divergent PII positive
control (an honestly-weak candidate, so it perturbs no ranking signal).
It carries the candidate's name in `summary` (the summary_emb boundary,
which no fixture exercised), name+email+phone verbatim in a header CHUNK
(embeddable text -- email/phone previously appeared only inside the
structured `candidate` block), and each of the three format-divergent
leak shapes ADR-007 round 4 closed: a line-broken name, a reflowed
phone, and a bare email local-part. Phase 3 took four audit rounds to
land that scrub and it had ZERO eval-corpus regression coverage.
--- Phase-4a strengthening additions (round 2: GAP 1 + GAP 2) ---
GAP 1 fix (expected_rank_band feasibility): a band is only useful if a
CORRECT ranker can actually satisfy it. Bands are now computed FROM the
corpus's tier population counts so they are feasible BY CONSTRUCTION,
walked in ascending-rank order. (Round 3 tiled ranks 1..N with no
gap/overlap; round 4 had to relax the TILING -- but not the feasibility
-- see the round-4 note below. Bands as of round 7 (17 fixtures: 7
strong / 4 borderline / 5 weak / 1 adversarial) were strong[1,7],
borderline[8,12], weak[12,null], adversarial[8,null]; round 8 below
RECOMPUTES these for a 20-fixture corpus -- see that note for the
current, authoritative values. Do not read the numbers in this
paragraph as current.)
`core/tests/unit/test_evals_corpus.py::test_expected_rank_bands_fit_tier_
populations` re-derives feasibility from the ACTUAL tag populations on
every run (Hall's condition over every contiguous rank window) and fails
if any set of fixtures is confined to fewer rank slots than there are
fixtures (this is exactly the bug that shipped in round 1:
expected_rank_band [1,3] for 'strong' while the corpus had 5 'strong'
fixtures -- no correct ranker could ever satisfy that). Whenever a
fixture's tag changes, recompute every band below.
--- Phase-4a FALSIFIABILITY hardening (round 4: finding B1) ---
The bands above were RE-DERIVED, because the round-3 corpus shipped a
DEFANGED adversarial bait and the bands encoded that defect.
r09 held a sub-bachelor 'Diploma, General Studies', which fails the JD's
education min_level ('bachelors') on its own. Measured against a
MatchWeights-faithful engine wired with a NO-OP evidence verifier, r09
scored 0.7878 -> rank 8: OUTSIDE the k=5 window. So the whole
[adversarial] arm was inert -- must_not_surface_in_topk PASSED and
precision@5 stayed 1.00 for an engine with no anti-fabrication check at
all. The education sub-score alone is 0.10 x 0.6 = 0.06 of score_final,
more than the 0.0485 gap between r09 and the top-5 cutoff: one
unasserted fixture field was doing the rejection work the EVIDENCE
verifier is supposed to do. r09 now holds a JD-allowed BSc Computer
Science (chunk c_006 narrates the same degree), and it is asserted --
along with the vector sub-score's embedded input -- by
test_r09_adversarial_bait_is_top_tier_on_every_non_evidence_signal.
Round 4 then claimed: 'with the bait repaired, the no-op-verifier engine
ranks r09 3rd -> precision@5 = 0.80 -> the adversarial arm correctly
FAILS it'. THAT NUMBER IS WRONG -- see round-5 F1. It was asserted, never
measured. Round 5 MEASURED the same corpus state: seniority 0.271 -> r09
rank 8 -> precision@5 = 1.00 -> the arm was STILL INERT. Round 4 did not
close the bait hole, it RELOCATED it onto seniority. (Round-7 finding M-1:
three files each stated a different, and false, rank for this one state --
'rank 2' in the test file, '3rd' here, '~11/17' in the docs. Each is now
marked wrong rather than quietly re-tuned; the narrative is unchanged.)
KNOCK-ON, and it is ARITHMETIC, not a mislabel: a candidate that is
top-tier on every NON-evidence signal and scores zero on evidence gets
score_final = 0.6*structured + 0.3*0 + 0.1*0, which lands it JUST BELOW
THE STRONG TIER -- NOT below every honestly-weak candidate. (Round 5
repaired the bait further and it now scores ~0.597; its exact rank is
near-tied with r04 and is NOT gated -- see r09's
expected_rank_band_note.) It is nowhere near the top-5 cutoff, so
every gate still bites. 'weak' and 'adversarial' therefore NO LONGER
SHARE A BAND: the bait gets its own, 'below every strong fixture and
therefore outside the top-k' -> [Nstrong+1, null] (round-8 note: this
was [8, null] against the 17-fixture corpus; see round 8 for the
current [10, null]). Because the bait consumes exactly one rank slot
inside the borderline/weak region and pushes whatever it outranks down
by one, the borderline band gains exactly ONE slot of slack over the
weak band's start. Do NOT 'fix' the overlap by weakening a threshold or
re-tagging r09.
--- Phase-4a FALSIFIABILITY hardening (round 5: F1 + F2) ---
Rounds 1-4 reasoned about an IDEALIZED engine. Round 5 read the one the
plan actually ports (hris packages/pipeline/src/pipeline/matching/
{stages,orchestrator}.py) and found TWO of the five structured
sub-scores do not compute what their names imply. Both bait-holes below
exist ONLY against the real algorithm:
F1 -- SENIORITY (0.15) is not a years check. orchestrator.py:331-340
computes cosine(jd.title, most-recent role title), rescaled from
[seniority_floor, 1] to [0, 1]. score_experience is the only sub-score
that reads years. But thresholds.toml and the potency test justified
BOTH experience (0.25) and seniority (0.15) with a single years-based
claim -- so the corpus asserted experience TWICE and seniority NEVER,
while r09 shipped 'Software Professional', the most JD-distant title of
any non-weak fixture. Measured (faithful engine + NO-OP verifier):
seniority 0.271 -> r09 rank 8 -> precision@5 = 1.00 -> A BAD ENGINE
PASSES. The round-4 fix did not close the bait hole; it RELOCATED it
from education (0.10) to seniority (0.15). r09's most-recent title is
now the JD title VERBATIM (also the most realistic keyword-stuffer
behaviour), so cosine(x, x) = 1.0 and seniority = 1.0 EXACTLY under any
embedder -- a guarantee by ARITHMETIC, not by measurement. That matters:
'Senior Backend Engineer' measured 0.755 on one nomic-embed-text build
and 0.581 on another, straddling the 0.638 break-even at which the trap
arms, so a merely-plausible title would leave this arm's arming
dependent on the embedding model.
F2 -- EDUCATION (0.10) reads the degree LEVEL only and NEVER reads
jd.education.fields, so the r14/r11 'education' ordering pair (twins
differing in FIELD) asserted a mechanism that does not exist and passed
an education-blind ranker via the embedded-degree vector leak. The twins
now differ in LEVEL. See ordering_controls[education].rationale.
OPEN DECISION for a human (recorded in docs/EXTRACTION_PLAN.md, NOT
silently resolved here): the JD fixture declares education.fields, the
ported score_education ignores them, so field-relevance is currently
DECORATIVE. Either extend the scorer to read fields (a NEW requirement,
not a port) or drop `fields` from the JD contract.
--- Phase-4a FALSIFIABILITY hardening (round 6: F5) ---
F5 -- TWO OF THE THREE ORDERING PAIRS DID NOT GATE THEIR DIMENSION. The
contract was rank(higher) < rank(lower) and nothing more, which is
satisfiable by a TIE-BREAK. Measured against an engine BLIND to each
pair's own dimension (real nomic-embed-text 768d + real rapidfuzz):
education   (weights.education = 0)   separation -3.266e-04
(-8.716e-04 after round 7 -- see ordering_controls[education] below)  FAIL/FAIL
overqual    (overqual_ratio = 99)     separation +0.000e+00  FAIL/PASS
motivation  (weights.motivation = 0)  separation +0.000e+00  PASS/FAIL
(verdicts given for the fixtures' natural order / the reversed order.)
So a MOTIVATION-BLIND ENGINE PASSED the motivation pair as the corpus
shipped, and the overqual pair failed only by tie-break luck.
ROOT CAUSE, and it is the mirror image of F2: _build_summary_text
(core/src/worker/resume_tasks.py) embeds summary/skills/experience/
education and NOTHING ELSE -- not total_years_experience, not
cover_letter_chunks, which are exactly the fields the overqual and
motivation twins differ in. Their embedding input is BYTE-IDENTICAL, so
their vector sub-scores are equal to the last bit, no residual exists to
break the tie, and stage4_combine's stable sort inherits stage-1's
ORDER BY vec_score DESC -- arbitrary for identical vectors. The overqual
rationale below BOASTS about the decision that creates this ('years/
seniority-neutral so the signal doesn't leak into summary_emb'): removing
the confound removed the tie-breaker. That byte-identity is still RIGHT --
the education pair only survives on ranks alone BECAUSE it keeps a
residual and F2 aimed it at the LOWER twin.
FIX (contract, not fixtures): thresholds.toml grows
[ordering_controls].min_score_gap = 1e-6, and the assertion becomes
rank(hi) < rank(lo) AND score_final(hi) - score_final(lo) >= min_score_gap.
An exact tie can then never pass under any tie-break, on any input order.
Correct-engine gaps: +0.0391 / +0.0120 / +0.0900. NOT fixed by copying
F2's inverted-residual trick into the other two twins: that would
re-introduce an embedder-dependent magnitude, which is the F1 lesson (pin
by arithmetic, not by measurement).
ROUND-7 CORRECTION (N-1): round 6 called all three of those gaps
'ARITHMETIC'. Only ONE is -- overqual (+0.0120 = 0.6*0.25*(1.00-0.92),
straight off MatchWeights and the twins' years). It is also the SMALLEST,
hence the one that bounds min_score_gap from above, and the only one the
corpus asserts. education (+0.0391) is an arithmetic 0.0400 less a
MEASURED vector residual; motivation (+0.0900 = 0.1 * 0.9) turns on the
LLM's MEASURED confidence for r04's cover letter, which is not a
MatchWeights constant at all.
--- Phase-4a FALSIFIABILITY hardening (round 7: R7-1 / R7-2) ---
R7-1 -- SKILL_EVIDENCE_MARKERS (test_evals_corpus.py) is the SOLE
definition of 'JD-relevant' for the corpus's core falsifiable property,
and its comment claimed it covered every required + nice-to-have skill.
NOTHING enforced that, so a JD skill without a marker was INVISIBLE to
the fabrication trap. Three mutations stayed green, the worst being: give
the JD a nice-to-have 'Redis' that r09 AND honest-strong r03 both claim
with zero textual support -- neither the 'adversarial must be ungrounded'
arm nor the 'honest must be grounded' arm fires. Coverage is now DERIVED
from the JD fixture (test_skill_evidence_markers_cover_every_jd_skill), so
a JD skill added by 4b/4d forces a marker in the same diff.
R7-2 -- the education twins' institution/year were unpinned, so the F2
residual could be INVERTED back and the education arm made inert again.
See ordering_controls[education].rationale for the measured mutation and
the fix (the twins now share an institution; the education dicts and the
embedded 'Education: ' segment are pinned to differ only in degree/field).
ROUND NUMBERING (round-7 finding N-3): rounds are counted CUMULATIVELY over
the corpus's hardening history -- rounds 1-2 on the original branch,
rounds 3-7 on fix/phase-4a-corpus-falsifiability. The branch's COMMIT
names count gate iterations on the branch, an offset of 2: cumulative
round 4 = red|green(4a-hard-2), round 5 = (4a-hard-3), round 6 =
(4a-hard-4), round 7 = (4a-hard-5). thresholds.toml, test_evals_corpus.py,
docs/activity and docs/EXTRACTION_PLAN.md all use the cumulative scheme.
GAP 2 fix (matched-pair 'ordering_controls'): r11 (education), r13
(overqual), and r04 (motivation) each only moved score WITHIN a tier,
so a ranker that ignored those dimensions still passed every invariant.
r14/r15/r16 are TWIN fixtures -- each identical to its partner in every
scoring-relevant field (skills/chunks/experience/years) EXCEPT the one
target dimension -- so that dimension is the SOLE differentiator between
the pair. `ordering_controls` below records, per pair, which member a
correct ranker must place strictly higher and why. The pairwise
ASSERTION itself -- rank(higher) < rank(lower) AND the score gap (F5) --
is a Phase-4c test (needs the live ranker); Phase 4a only guarantees the
twins are genuinely 'identical except X' via the per-pair integrity tests
in test_evals_corpus.py, which is the thing that makes the eventual 4c
assertion trustworthy rather than confounded.
--- Phase-4c PREP: skill-sub-score twins + mutation scaffolding (round 8) ---
Scope: docs/EXTRACTION_PLAN.md's 4b->4c BLOCKERS section (2026-07-14) and
the R1/R2 residuals it carries forward. R1 said the corpus is 'blind to
the internals of the skill sub-score' -- weights.skill=0,
must_have_miss_penalty:0.5->1.0, and recency-decay-disabled all PASSED
the 17-fixture corpus. This round adds THREE new fixtures and TWO new
ordering_controls pairs to close as much of that as a fixture-only
change can, and documents in writing what still can't be closed without
the live engine (core/tests/evals/README_4c_twins.md carries the full
writeup; this note is the short version for anyone reading labels.json
alone).
1) r18_casey_rivera_missing_must_have -- byte-for-byte r01 MINUS the
'REST API design' skill entry (nothing else changed: same summary,
chunks, experience, education). REST API design has NO family in
categories.yaml (src/pipeline/skill_data/categories.yaml), so its
absence is an UNAMBIGUOUS ontology_weight=0 genuine miss -- there is no
family-credit path for this skill at all, unlike Apache Airflow (whose
family 'data' is shared with Python -- see the finding below). Paired
against r01 (dimension 'skill_missing_must' in ordering_controls): a
correct engine scores r01's skill_overall = 1.00 (5/5 exact matches,
all recent) and r18's = 0.8 pre-penalty (4/5, one missing) x
must_have_miss_penalty(0.5) = 0.40 -- gap 0.60 in skill units, 0.144 in
score_final units (0.6*0.40*0.60). Tagged 'borderline' (a fixture that
is otherwise strong-caliber but genuinely lacks one must-have is
expected to land mid-tier, not in the strong band and not among the
weak/adversarial fixtures that lack most of the JD outright).
FINDING (round 8, provable without an embedder): the
must_have_miss_penalty:0.5->1.0 mutation CANNOT be made to fail this
(or any) pairwise ordering_controls comparison by reversing rank or
collapsing below min_score_gap, and this is a property of the
algorithm's ARITHMETIC, not a fixture design failure. Removing the
penalty changes r18's score from 0.8*0.5=0.40 to 0.8*1.0=0.80 -- the
CANNOT reverse or reach zero, because a genuinely-missing row is FORCED
to contribute exactly 0.0 to the pre-penalty mean (stages.py:
'if ontology_weight==0: score=0.0'), which is strictly less than any
present skill's contribution regardless of the penalty multiplier. The
raw (pre-penalty) mean difference alone (1.00 vs 0.80, i.e. 1 row out of
5) survives ANY value of must_have_miss_penalty, including 1.0. THIS
MUTATION THEREFORE CANNOT BE GATED BY A PAIRWISE RANK+GAP CHECK, EVER,
for a 'present vs genuinely-absent' twin design -- unlike the education/
overqual/motivation mutations, which the existing ordering_controls
mechanism CAN express. 4c's reviewer must instead verify
must_have_miss_penalty numerically on r18 ALONE: score_final(r18,
must_have_miss_penalty=0.5) must be measurably LOWER than
score_final(r18, must_have_miss_penalty=1.0) by approximately 0.048
(0.6*0.40*0.20), confirming the penalty is wired and fires at all. This
is a REVIEW OBLIGATION, not a gate this file or thresholds.toml can
express (same class as the round-7 M-3 obligations below) -- recorded
here and in README_4c_twins.md so it isn't silently dropped.
weights.skill=0 DOES gate this pair (unlike the penalty mutation): it
deletes the entire 0.144 arithmetic gap, leaving only the residual from
the embedded 'Skills:' line differing by one dropped token -- far
smaller than any measured residual elsewhere in this corpus. 4c must
MEASURE (not assume) which way that residual points before trusting
this pair's weights.skill=0 verdict at the min_score_gap boundary (the
same discipline round 6/7 already applied to the education pair).
2) r19_jamie_okafor_recency_twin -- byte-for-byte r10 with EVERY skill's
last_used_year moved from the old bucket (2017/2018) to the recent
bucket (2026); summary, experience (incl. start/end dates), education,
and chunks are UNCHANGED. _build_summary_text embeds neither
last_used_year nor experience start/end dates, so r19's embedding input
is BYTE-IDENTICAL to r10's -- exactly the F5 technique already used for
the overqual/motivation pairs, and stronger than the r01/r18 pair above
(no residual at all, not even a small one). Paired against r10
(dimension 'recency' in ordering_controls): a correct engine scores
r10's skill_overall = 0.40 (5/5 present, all in the recency_old bucket,
recency=0.4) and r19's = 1.00 (same 5/5, recency=1.0) -- gap 0.60 in
skill units, 0.144 in score_final units (0.6*0.40*0.60), identical in
magnitude to the r01/r18 gap by coincidence of both being a single
full-weight skill-row swing of 0.6 (not the same mechanism: this one is
a recency multiplier change 1.0-vs-0.4, not a missing-row penalty).
Because the embedding input ties EXACTLY, BOTH weights.skill=0 AND
recency-decay-disabled (recency forced to 1.0 regardless of
last_used_year) collapse this pair to an EXACT tie (separation
0.000e+00 by construction, not by measurement) -- both mutations FAIL
deterministically, no embedder measurement required. This is the
strongest of the three new falsifiability additions.
Tagged 'borderline', matching r10's own tag (house convention: a
matched pair shares one tag, same as the education/overqual/motivation
pairs -- the pairwise rank+gap check, not the tag boundary, does the
ordering work). See README_4c_twins.md for the caveat that the
arithmetic-only 0.144 gap has not been measured against a real
embedder, so r19's true position within (or just above) the
borderline band is not independently confirmed.
NARRATIVE CAVEAT (deliberate, matching the overqual pair's precedent of
accepting a 'neutral' summary for isolation purity): r19's summary text
still narrates work 'concluding in 2018' even though its skills'
last_used_year is now 2026. This inconsistency is intentional -- 'all
else pinned identical' was read literally so the byte-identical-
embedding guarantee holds -- and is cosmetic only; it is not read by
the recency scorer, which looks at skills[].last_used_year, never at
summary prose.
3) r20_casey_rivera_spelling_twin -- byte-for-byte r01 except the
'REST API design' skill entry's name is spelled 'REST APIs' (years/
last_used_year/evidence_chunk_ids unchanged). Both spellings resolve
to the SAME canonical concept 'rest api design' via
src/pipeline/skill_data/aliases.yaml's alias list (['rest api design',
'rest api', 'rest apis', 'restful api', 'restful apis']) -- the
post-4b spelling-recall fix ADR-008 residual #6 records. This is NOT
an ordering_controls pair (r01 and r20 should TIE, not rank one above
the other -- ordering_controls' rank(higher)<rank(lower) contract has
no way to express 'approximately equal'). Instead it is gated by the
EXISTING expected_rank_band mechanism: r20 is tagged 'strong' with the
same band as r01, so if a future regression removes 'rest apis' from
the alias table, r20's skill sub-score reverts to the pre-fix
ontology_weight=0 genuine-miss case (measured historically at -0.144 on
score_final, ADR-008 residual #6) -- large enough, given the
strong/borderline margins recorded elsewhere in this corpus's history
(~0.05-0.16), to plausibly push r20 OUT of the strong band on its own,
which test_every_label_entry_has_an_expected_rank_band_matching_its_tag
(once wired to a live ranker) would catch. 4c's reviewer should ALSO
run the explicit mutation (delete the 'rest apis'/'restful api(s)'
aliases from aliases.yaml's rest-api-design entry) and confirm r20's
score_final drops by approximately 0.144 and/or its rank leaves the
strong band -- recorded as a review obligation, not a gate this file
can express, mirroring the round-7 M-3 pattern.
POPULATION / BAND RECOMPUTE (mandatory per the round-2 rule: 'whenever a
fixture's tag changes, recompute every band below'). Adding r18
(strong -- tagged to match its ordering_controls partner r01, per
this corpus's house convention that a matched pair shares one tag),
r19 (borderline -- matching its partner r10, same convention), and
r20 (strong, no pairing constraint) changes the tier populations
from 7/4/5/1 (round 7, 17 fixtures) to 9/5/5/1 (round 8, 20 fixtures):
strong=9, borderline=5, weak=5, adversarial=1. Recomputed bands (same
derivation as round 2/4): strong=[1,9], borderline=[10,15],
weak=[15,null], adversarial=[10,null]. EVERY existing entry's
expected_rank_band below has been updated to match its tag's new
canonical band (not just the three new entries) so this file stays
internally consistent with its own documented derivation algorithm.
r09's expected_rank_band_note has had its rank-slot arithmetic updated
(Nstrong+1: 8 -> 10) but its SCORE-based claims (~0.597, ~0.785 cutoff,
~0.19 margin, the 2.8e-04 r04 near-tie) are UNCHANGED because they were
measured against the 17-fixture corpus and this round has no engine to
re-measure them with -- re-verify before trusting them at that
precision against the 20-fixture corpus.
core/tests/unit/test_evals_corpus.py's `_TAG_POPULATIONS_AT_AUTHORING_
TIME` (7/4/5/1) and the `TAG_RANK_BANDS` it derives are a HARDCODED
constant in that file, which this round's tester does NOT own and did
NOT modify (explicit task boundary: fixtures/labels.json/thresholds.toml
only). Landing this round's fixtures WITHOUT a companion update to that
constant (7/4/5/1 -> 9/5/5/1) will fail
test_every_label_entry_has_an_expected_rank_band_matching_its_tag AND
test_expected_rank_bands_fit_tier_populations for every 'strong'/
'borderline' entry (old vs new bands disagree) -- THIS IS EXPECTED AND
REQUIRED, not a bug in this file: it is the coder's signal to update
that constant in the same landing diff, exactly like round 4's
[adversarial] fix already had to rework the tiling once before. See
README_4c_twins.md for the exact replacement values.
FAKE_NAMES (test_evals_corpus.py): r18/r20 reuse 'Casey Rivera' (r01's
name) and r19 reuses 'Jamie Okafor' (r10's name) -- both already on the
allowlist -- specifically so this round does not need to touch that
constant either. This is a deliberate scope-boundary choice (this
round's tester owns labels.json/fixtures/thresholds.toml, not
test_evals_corpus.py), not an oversight; nothing in the corpus asserts

GOLD-EVIDENCE RECALL (R2 closure): thresholds.toml gains
[evidence].gold_recall_min = 1.0 -- see that file's comment for the
full rationale (stage-3 recall, not just verify-stage precision). No

'weak'. r09 is top-tier on every NON-evidence signal, all five as the
ENGINE computes them: all 5 required + all 3 nice-to-have skills, every
years >= min_years, every last_used_year in the recency_recent bucket;
clears min_years_experience without tripping overqual_ratio
(score_experience = 1.00); its most-recent role title is the JD title
VERBATIM, so the seniority cosine is 1.0 and the sub-score is 1.00
EXACTLY under any embedder; a bachelor's meeting the JD min_level
(education = 1.00); every JD skill named in the embedded summary
(vector = 0.96). Measured structured = 0.9953 -- essentially a perfect
structured candidate.
So score_final = 0.6*0.9953 + 0.3*0 + 0.1*0 = 0.597 and it lands JUST
BELOW THE STRONG TIER, not below every honestly-weak candidate. That
is arithmetic, not a mislabel. What the band still gates, hard: min =
Nstrong+1 = 10 (round-8 update: Nstrong is now 9, was 7/8 through
round 7 -- see the round-8 note above), i.e. the bait must rank below
EVERY strong fixture and therefore outside the k=5 shortlist (margin:
~0.597 vs the ~0.785 5th-place cutoff = ~0.19).
THE EXACT RANK IS NOT GATED AND IS NOT BUILD-STABLE -- do not re-pin
one here (round-6 reconciliation). r09 and r04 are separated by 2.8e-04
(0.596994 vs 0.596711), so which of them takes rank 8 flips between
nomic-embed-text builds. Both stay in band either way (adversarial
admits [10, null], borderline [10, 15]) and the ~0.19 margin below the
top-5 cutoff is unchanged. The near-tie is a CONSEQUENCE of the
arithmetic below, not a defect.
ROUND-8 CAVEAT: the ~0.597 / ~0.785 / ~0.19 / 2.8e-04 figures above were
measured against the 17-fixture corpus, before r18/r19/r20 were added.
None of those three affects r09's OWN score (it is untouched), but the
'5th-place cutoff' could shift if r19/r20 outscore whichever fixture
previously held rank 5 -- this has not been re-measured with a real

ROUND-5 FINDING F1: before this, r09's title was 'Software
Professional' -- the most JD-DISTANT title of any non-weak fixture --
and NOTHING asserted it, because the potency test justified both the

seniority does not read years). Measured with a NO-OP evidence
verifier: seniority 0.271 -> r09 rank 8 -> precision@5 = 1.00 -> a bad
engine PASSED. The trap fires iff seniority(r09) >= 0.638. With the JD
title, a no-op-verifier engine now ranks r09 FIRST (precision@5 = 0.80
-> FAIL), which is the strongest possible statement of the trap.
WHY THE NEAR-TIE WITH r04 IS EXPECTED (and why the band is a BAND): a
candidate that is perfect on structure and zero on evidence scores
0.6 * ~1.0 by construction, which is close to what an honest borderline
candidate scores by a different route. The two are within ~5e-04 of each
other and the sign of that difference is build-dependent (round 5
measured the bait 0.0005 BELOW r04; the round-6 re-audit, on a different
nomic-embed-text build, measured it 0.00028 ABOVE). Nothing gates it.
Do NOT chase the sign of that residual by editing fixtures.

ordering_controls.rationale: r14 and r11 are identical in skills, experience, total_years_experience, summary, AND their FULL chunk list. They differ ONLY in the structured education[] entry -- and WITHIN that entry, only in `degree` and `field` (they SHARE an institution and a year: round-7 finding R7-2, below). The degree carries the LEVEL, which is the only thing the ported scorer reads: r14 holds a bachelor's (BSc Computer Science -> level 'bachelors' = 3 >= the JD's min_level 3 -> education sub-score 1.00); r11 holds a sub-bachelor associate credential (Associate Degree in Data Engineering -> level 'associate' = 2 < 3 -> education sub-score = education_partial * 2/3 = 0.333). BOTH fields are JD-ALLOWED (Computer Science / Data Engineering), deliberately: the field must not be a second differentiator, and that also makes this pair survive EITHER resolution of the open 4c decision on whether score_education should read jd.education.fields at all. ROUND-5 FIX (finding F2) -- THIS PAIR DID NOT TEST EDUCATION. It previously claimed the twins differed in the education FIELD (r14 Computer Science vs r11 Mechanical Engineering) and that MatchWeights.education_partial (0.5) would demote r11. That mechanism DOES NOT EXIST: stages.score_education() reads the degree LEVEL and NEVER reads jd.education.fields, so both twins were BSc -> 'bachelors' -> education = 1.00 for BOTH and education_partial could never fire. Worse, the pair still PASSED an education-blind ranker -- through the VECTOR path: core/src/worker/resume_tasks.py::_build_summary_text embeds education[].degree + institution into summary_emb, so the degree difference leaked into the vector sub-score, and with the education sub-score DELETED outright (weights.education = 0.0) r14 still outranked r11. The entire gap was vector. That is the D1 confound round 3 believed it had closed by deleting the education CHUNK -- but the degree still rode into summary_emb via the structured education[] entry. A differing LEVEL necessarily means a differing degree STRING, so that vector residual cannot be removed; it is instead DOMINATED (education moves score_final by 0.6 * 0.10 * 0.667 = 0.040, vs the residual's 0.00087) and pointed the OTHER WAY -- r11's 'Data Engineering' degree text embeds CLOSER to the JD than r14's 'Computer Science', so the residual favours the LOWER twin. Consequence, and it is the point: the ONLY way an engine can place r14 above r11 is by actually implementing the education sub-score. Measured (faithful engine, real embedder): correct engine -> r14 rank 3, r11 rank 7, gap +0.039128 (0.6 * 0.10 * (1 - education_partial * 2/3) = 0.0400, less the 0.00087 vector residual); weights.education = 0.0 -> the pair FLIPS (r11 rank 3 above r14 rank 4, separation -8.716e-04) -> FAIL, on BOTH input orders. That mutation is a REVIEW OBLIGATION on the 4c PR, not something thresholds.toml can gate (round-7 finding M-3): it needs the engine run with MUTATED MatchWeights, so it belongs in 4c's test suite and 4c's reviewer must check for it. ROUND-7 FINDING R7-2 -- THE RESIDUAL'S SIGN IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF OF ALL OF THIS, IT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARITHMETIC, AND ITS INPUTS WERE UNPINNED. _build_summary_text embeds the education entry as `{degree}, {institution} ({year})`; the twin test pinned skills/experience/summary/chunks/years and NONE of those three, and test_twins_that_share_an_embedding_input_... compares only the segment BEFORE 'Education: '. The twins even shipped DIFFERENT institutions ('Fredericton Polytechnic College' vs 'Fredericton Institute of Technology') for no stated reason. Measured mutation: rewrite r14's institution to 'Backend Data Engineering Institute of Python and Airflow' and the raw residual flips to +0.0043, the education-BLIND engine's twin separation becomes +6.399e-04 >= [ordering_controls].min_score_gap, and the blind engine PASSES this pair on BOTH input orders -- i.e. the exact vector confound F2 was fixed to invert is re-created, and every corpus test stays green. FIX: the twins now SHARE an institution and a year, and test_r14_education_twin_is_identical_to_r11_except_education_level asserts (a) the two education dicts are equal except `degree`/`field` and (b) the embedded 'Education: ' segment differs ONLY in the degree token -- so the degree TEXT is the residual's sole contributor and the institution can never silently become a second one. Unifying the institution moved NO rank anywhere in the corpus (r11 0.7578 -> 0.7583, still rank 7) and STRENGTHENED the inversion (residual -3.30e-04 -> -8.72e-04). Whoever changes a twin's institution/year/degree again: re-measure the education-blind separation and re-derive the bands, in the same diff. ROUND-6 (finding F5): this is the ONLY one of the three pairs whose blind engine is genuinely SEPARATED (the other two tie EXACTLY, because their twins' embedding input is byte-identical), so it is the only one a rank-only assertion could ever have gated -- it works BECAUSE the residual above exists and points at the LOWER twin. The pairwise assertion is now rank AND gap for all three pairs alike: rank(r14) < rank(r11) AND score_final(r14) - score_final(r11) >= [ordering_controls].min_score_gap (1e-6). LANDMINE for whoever edits r11's degree string: orchestrator._level_from_degree substring-matches in priority order and the MASTERS bucket contains the keyword 'ma ' (trailing space), tested BEFORE 'associate' -- so 'Associate Diploma in Data Engineering' contains 'diplo-MA -in' and maps to MASTERS (level 4 -> education 1.00), silently re-confounding this pair. test_r11_degree_string_does_not_collide_with_a_higher_level_keyword pins it.

r15 and r13 are identical in skills, cited chunks, experience, education, AND summary. The summary is deliberately years/seniority-neutral: total_years_experience is NOT embedded by _build_summary_text, so if the summary narrated the years or 'overqualified' it would become the SOLE embedded differentiator and leak the overqual signal into summary_emb (the vector sub-score) -- letting a no-op overqual penalty pass 4c's ordering assertion via the vector path. They differ ONLY in total_years_experience: r15=6 gives ratio 6/5=1.2 (< MatchWeights.overqual_ratio=2.0), so NOT overqualified; r13=14 gives ratio 14/5=2.8 (>= overqual_ratio), triggering the overqual penalty (slope/floor). Every embedded field now matches, so any score gap must come from the structured overqual penalty alone. ROUND-6 FIX (finding F5) -- AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY THE RANK-ONLY ASSERTION GATED NOTHING HERE. Because the twins' embedding input is byte-identical, an engine BLIND to the overqual penalty (overqual_ratio = 99, so it never fires) scores them an EXACT TIE (separation +0.000e+00, measured to 10 decimals), and stage4_combine's stable sort then decides the pair by stage-1's ORDER BY vec_score DESC -- arbitrary for identical vectors. Measured: the blind engine FAILS the pair in the fixtures' natural order but PASSES it on the reversed order. The pair was a coin flip. The byte-identity stays (it is the right call); the ASSERTION is what changed: 4c must check rank(r15) < rank(r13) AND score_final(r15) - score_final(r13) >= [ordering_controls].min_score_gap (1e-6). A tie then fails on BOTH input orders. The correct engine's gap here is 0.6 * 0.25 * (1.00 - 0.92) = +0.0120 EXACTLY -- pure arithmetic off MatchWeights, no embedder in it, and the smallest of the three pairs' gaps (which is what bounds min_score_gap from above). 4c MUST run the overqual_ratio = 99 mutation and confirm it FAILS on both input orders. Do NOT 'fix' the tie by narrating the years into r15's summary: that re-introduces an embedder-dependent vector differentiator and turns this back into a pair a penalty-blind ranker passes (finding F2, on the education pair). test_twins_that_share_an_embedding_input_are_the_reason_min_score_gap_exists pins it.

r04 and r16 are identical in skills, cited chunks, experience, education, and total_years_experience. r04 carries non-empty cover_letter_chunks (genuine motivation/role-alignment evidence); r16 has NO cover letter at all. MatchWeights.motivation (0.1 top-level weight) should rank r04 strictly above r16 -- previously r04 was the corpus's ONLY cover-letter fixture, so motivation had no second candidate to be ranked against and could not be gated at all. ROUND-6 FIX (finding F5) -- THIS PAIR PASSED A MOTIVATION-BLIND ENGINE, in the fixtures' natural order, right up to this change. _build_summary_text does not read cover_letter_chunks (only summary/skills/experience/education), so these twins' embedding input is BYTE-IDENTICAL and their vector sub-scores are equal to the last bit. With weights.motivation = 0 the twins' score_final is an EXACT TIE (separation +0.000e+00), and rank(r04) < rank(r16) was then decided purely by stage4_combine's stable sort inheriting stage-1's ORDER BY vec_score DESC -- which for identical vectors is arbitrary, and which happened to favour r04. Reverse the input order and the same blind engine FAILS. The pair was a coin flip that landed the right way up. Fixed in the CONTRACT, not the fixtures: 4c must assert rank(r04) < rank(r16) AND score_final(r04) - score_final(r16) >= [ordering_controls].min_score_gap (1e-6), which no tie can satisfy on any input order. The correct engine's gap is 0.1 * 0.9 = +0.0900 (the motivation weight times the verified cover-letter confidence), four orders of magnitude clear. 4c MUST run the weights.motivation = 0 mutation and confirm it FAILS on BOTH input orders. Do NOT 'fix' the tie by narrating motivation into r04's summary -- that leaks the signal into summary_emb and makes this a vector test (finding F2).

ROUND-8 ADDITION (4c blocker #1/#2a, docs/EXTRACTION_PLAN.md; closes half of R1 -- 'the corpus is blind to the internals of the skill sub-score'). r18 is byte-for-byte r01 MINUS the 'REST API design' skill entry; nothing else (summary, chunks, experience, education, the other 4 skill entries) differs. REST API design carries NO family in src/pipeline/skill_data/categories.yaml, so its absence resolves to an ontology_weight=0 GENUINE miss with no possible family-credit path -- unlike Apache Airflow, whose family 'data' is shared with Python (categories.yaml lists both under `data`), so ANY candidate holding Python (a separate required must-have) automatically gets family credit toward a missing Airflow row and can never demonstrate a clean ontology_weight=0 for that skill specifically (this is the exact mechanism r04/r16 already exhibit against a real family-credit-aware engine, per docs/EXTRACTION_PLAN.md's blocker #1 -- +0.1120 measured on score_final, of which +0.1000 is the missing-must penalty going silent). REST API design was chosen over Airflow for THIS pair specifically because it has no family at all, so the 'genuine miss' half is unambiguous by construction rather than by careful non-overlap engineering. Correct engine: r01's must list is 5/5 present, all recent, all years-sufficient -> skill_overall = 1.00, missing_must = [] -> no penalty -> final skill contribution 1.00. r18's must list is 4/5 present (REST API design row forced to score=0.0 per stages.py's `if ontology_weight==0: score=0.0`) -> mean 0.8, missing_must=[REST API design] (nonempty under EITHER the current score==0.0 check OR docs/EXTRACTION_PLAN.md's recommended ontology_weight==0 fix, since this row is 0 under both) -> not senior (r18's total_years_experience=6 < 5*implied_seniority_factor(1.5)=7.5) -> must_have_miss_penalty(0.5) applies -> 0.8*0.5=0.40. Gap = 1.00-0.40=0.60 in skill units, 0.6*0.40*0.60=0.144 in score_final units -- the largest gap of any ordering pair in this corpus, and independently derived from the SAME arithmetic that produced ADR-008 residual #6's measured -0.144 spelling-regression figure (a coincidence of magnitude, not mechanism: that regression is a spelling non-match; this pair is a genuine, spelling-irrelevant absence -- both happen to be 'one of five required rows flips from ontology_weight=1.0 to 0.0', hence the matching number). weights.skill=0 GATES this pair: it deletes the entire 0.144 gap, leaving only the tiny vector residual from the embedded 'Skills:' line dropping one token -- 4c must MEASURE (not assume) that residual's sign before trusting this pair's weights.skill=0 verdict at the min_score_gap boundary, same discipline as the education pair. must_have_miss_penalty:0.5->1.0 does NOT and PROVABLY CANNOT reverse or collapse this (or any) pairwise comparison built as 'present vs genuinely-absent': removing the penalty changes r18's score from 0.8*0.5=0.40 to 0.8*1.0=0.80, shrinking the gap to 0.6*0.40*0.20=0.048 (a real, ~3x reduction) but never past zero, because the pre-penalty raw mean difference (1.00 vs 0.80, from the one forced-zero row) survives ANY penalty value including 1.0 -- this is arithmetic, not a fixture defect, and it means the pairwise rank+gap mechanism this file's ordering_controls uses CANNOT express a must_have_miss_penalty mutation test for ANY twin of this shape. 4c's reviewer must instead verify the penalty numerically on r18 in isolation: score_final(r18, penalty=0.5) must be measurably lower than score_final(r18, penalty=1.0) by approximately 0.048 (0.6*0.40*0.20) -- a REVIEW OBLIGATION recorded here and in README_4c_twins.md, not something thresholds.toml or this pairwise mechanism can gate (same class as the round-7 M-3 obligations above).

ROUND-8 ADDITION (4c blocker #2b, docs/EXTRACTION_PLAN.md; closes the other half of R1 -- r10's decision_point 'recency_decay_stale_skills' was decorative through round 7 because no fixture isolated it). r19 is byte-for-byte r10 with every skill's last_used_year moved from the old bucket (2017/2018) to the recent bucket (2026); summary, experience (including start/end dates), education, and chunks are UNCHANGED. _build_summary_text (core/src/worker/resume_tasks.py) reads neither last_used_year nor experience start/end dates, so r19's embedding input is BYTE-IDENTICAL to r10's -- stronger than the r01/r18 pair above (which has a small, unmeasured vector residual from a dropped skill token) and matching the technique that makes the overqual/motivation pairs airtight. Correct engine: r10's 5 required skills are all present with sufficient years but last_used_year in the recency_old bucket (delta > MatchWeights.recency_mid_years=5 -> recency=recency_old=0.4) -> skill_overall = mean(5 rows, each years_score=1.0 * recency=0.4 * ontology_weight=1.0 = 0.4) = 0.40. r19's identical rows but recency_recent bucket (delta<=recency_recent_years=2 -> recency=1.0) -> skill_overall = 1.00. Gap = 0.60 in skill units, 0.6*0.40*0.60=0.144 in score_final units. BECAUSE the embedding input ties EXACTLY and experience/education/total_years_experience are also unchanged between the twins, BOTH weights.skill=0 AND a recency-decay-disabled mutation (recency forced to a constant 1.0 regardless of last_used_year, e.g. via MatchWeights.recency_recent=recency_mid=recency_old=1.0) collapse every remaining sub-score to an EXACT tie between r19 and r10 -- separation 0.000e+00 BY CONSTRUCTION, not by measurement, so both mutations FAIL this pair on BOTH input orders with no embedder-dependent uncertainty at all (unlike every other pair in this corpus, including the new skill_missing_must pair above). 4c MUST run both the weights.skill=0 and the recency-decay-disabled mutation and confirm each fails deterministically. NARRATIVE CAVEAT: r19's summary still narrates hands-on work 'concluding in 2018' even though its skills now carry last_used_year=2026 -- a deliberate, cosmetic inconsistency accepted (matching the overqual pair's precedent of a values-neutral summary) so 'all else pinned identical' could be read literally and the byte-identical-embedding guarantee could hold without qualification; the recency scorer reads only skills[].last_used_year, never summary prose, so this does not affect the mechanism being tested.
